picks.what_it_is: Original watercolour of a thylacine on a rock in a Tasmanian bush setting, signed lower left (reads as M.F. PLEDGER on an enlarged crop), with two typed letters signed Maurice Pledger about the Tassie Tiger commission and a Hobart exhibition at the Masterpiece Gallery. Timber frame, double mat.
picks.working: No comps. The valuer found no sold Pledger originals and my own search was blocked (WebSearch budget 200/200 used). No sold price with a URL and date, so no calculation and no maximum bid. Kept as a near miss only because the identification is strong and the subject is appealing to Tasmanian bidders.
picks.condition: Appears good in photos, no obvious foxing or staining visible. Not checked under glass.
picks.key_photo_findings: Signature on the painting is small but reads as M.F. PLEDGER, matching the letters signed Maurice F Pledger. Letter says he painted the tiger in a Tasmanian setting as a commission and mentions a friend John Norwood relaying commissions. Small handwritten label top right of the mat is not legible.
picks.question_for_armitage: Is it a watercolour or gouache, and what is the sight size? Are the two letters original signed letters (not copies) and do they go with the painting? Any foxing or damage under the glass? What does the small label on the mat say?
